conventions.convention: The root inner product is linear in its first argument; Dirac bras act by z ↦ ⟨z,x⟩root.
The clean injection is Jx = |0A⟩ ⊗ x. Every coefficient and PREPARE-work ancilla belongs to the zero projection. A zero-weight branch has no assigned conditional vector.

LCU normalization is the sum of absolute values of the listed coefficients, with α > 0. SELECT includes coefficient phases and is identity on padded indices. PREPARE may prepare the coefficient vector up to a single global phase.

The oblivious reflection is R0 = I − 2JJ†, the opposite of the supplier's RΠ = 2Π − I. The amplified circuit includes the explicit scalar correction C = −WR0W†R0W; under control the correction is a relative phase.
Taylor order K includes degrees 0 through K. Ordered tuples remain distinct entries, and tuple (j1,…,jk) represents Vj1⋯Vjk. Two cancelling identity entries set the listed normalization to 2.

Each segment receives fresh zero-initialized coefficient/work registers, and all are retained in the output dilation. The guarantee is a clean-input isometry bound, not exact ancilla restoration or a full-space approximation on dirty inputs.

One indexed term query requires an explicitly supplied coherent term multiplexer and its needed controls/inverses. Assembly from separate controlled terms costs up to m individual calls per indexed query; routing, phases, arithmetic and generation are separately charged.

load_bearing.statement: For a nonzero finite-dimensional system, unitary W with J†WJ = M/2, unitary V, and ‖M−V‖ ≤ η ≤ 1/100, the phase-corrected circuit C = −WR0W†R0W satisfies ‖CJ−JV‖ ≤ 10√η, including residual ancilla leakage.

For the supplied finite LCU circuit W and full clean injection J, J†WJ = M/α. For unit ψ the zero-branch vector is Mψ/α, its weight is ‖Mψ‖²/α², and its normalized conditional vector is Mψ/‖Mψ‖ when that weight is positive; otherwise it is undefined.

For the stated finite Hermitian-unitary decomposition on a nonzero space, real h, K ≥ 0 and x = Λ|h|, ‖MK(h)−e^(−ihH)‖ ≤ e^x x^(K+1)/(K+1)!. If x ≤ ln 2 then sK ≤ e^x ≤ 2, and for 0 < η < 1 an order K = O(1 + log(1/η)/log log(e+1/η)) makes the bound at most η.
If W is unitary, J†WJ = M/2 and R0 = I−2JJ†, then J†WR0W†R0WJ = −3M/2 + MM†M/2. For unitary M this is −M; the identity alone supplies no leakage estimate for nonunitary M.
For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces HA, HE and Hermitian X on HA ⊗ HE, ‖TrE X‖1 ≤ ‖X‖1. If either factor is zero-dimensional, both sides are zero.
For unit vectors u,v in a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, D(Pu,Pv) := ½‖Pu−Pv‖1 ≤ ‖u−v‖.

seams_checked.note: The LCU access definition uses the exact preparation algorithm and its O((q+1)D) continuous-rotation bound, permits a global phase, includes workspace and separates table arithmetic and finite-alphabet compilation.

The cited model supplies separate resource coordinates. The Taylor result explicitly states a retained-work clean-input isometry guarantee and does not claim exact ancilla restoration or the supplier's target-only unitary interface.
Exact clean/dirty return contracts remain distinct from zero initialization. Taylor output registers are explicitly retained with leakage rather than asserted to be exact clean ancillas.
Forward, inverse and controlled access remain separate. The opposite reflection sign and required control-Z correction are stated, and the OAA minus sign is tracked under control.
The circuit-cost definition is used for separate queries, gates, widths, descriptions and generation costs; no efficient full-list compiler follows from interval names or matrix data.
Dirac translation and domain-based singular-value trace norms are preserved. The pure-state and Hermitian partial-trace arguments derive their additional bounds locally.
Ancilla-first injections, ordered product coordinates and contraction over discarded factors agree with the suppliers. Zero-factor and zero-qubit cases are distinguished.
The isometry and projector suppliers are used only for inner-product preservation, J†J = I and the orthogonal projection JJ†. Their finite-dimensional and pairing hypotheses match.

The qubitized algorithm step 5 and correctness theorem F10/step 2.1 use the complete phase-corrected OAA circuit with clean block Mph/2. Their ηOAA ≤ (3ε/128)² < 1/100 satisfies the robust lemma, giving 10√ηOAA ≤ 15ε/64 including retained-work leakage.
